name: Question 1
problem: Given that $f(x,y)=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{y}),$ find the set of values $(x,y)$ on which $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ exists.
worked_solution:
First, notice that $f(x,y)$ is not defined when $y=0.$ So, the domain of $f$ is 

$$
{D}_{f}={(x,y)\,:\,y\ne 0}.
$$

Now, we compute the partial derivatives of $f(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{y})) \\  & =\frac{-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}}{1+{(\frac{x}{y})}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

The function ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ is not defined at the point $(0,0).$ So, the domain of ${f}_{y}$ is

$$
{D}_{{f}_{y}}={(x,y)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\ne 0}.
$$

Finally, we conclude that the partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $y$ exists on the set

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{f}\cap {D}_{{f}_{y}} & ={(x,y)\,:\,y\ne 0}\cap {(x,y)\,:\,{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\ne 0} \\  & ={(x,y)\,:\,y\ne 0}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Given that f(x,y)=arctan⁡(xy), find the set of values (x,y) on which ∂f∂y exists.

a
fy exists everywhere on the xy-plane
b
{(x,y):x≠0}
c
{(x,y):y≠0}
d
{(x,y):y≠−x}
e
{(x,y):y≠x}
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, notice that f(x,y) is not defined when y=0. So, the domain of f is Df={(x,y):y≠0}.

Now, we compute the partial derivatives of f(x,y) with respect to y:

fy(x,y)=∂∂y(arctan⁡(xy))=−xy21+(xy)2=−xy2+x2

The function fy(x,y) is not defined at the point (0,0). So, the domain of fy is

Dfy={(x,y):x2+y2≠0}.

Finally, we conclude that the partial derivative of f with respect to y exists on the set

Df∩Dfy={(x,y):y≠0}∩{(x,y):x2+y2≠0}={(x,y):y≠0}.
